- `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` read by symbol on `origin/main = a39b02a6`: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:7692` = `'claude-fable-5'`. Same mismatch, third seat.

Posture this seat records for its five in-flight Clause-② cards (#13802 · #14106 · #14153 · #13671 · #13672), auditable in the seat body: the fuse is read as the floor it was written to be — a guard against silent downgrade — and `claude-fable-5-1` is the successor point release of the constant's family, not a lower tier, so this seat performs the in-seat contract review itself per the 2026-08-31 ruling and writes the exact served string (`claude-fable-5-1`) plus the constant's value into every PASS/FAIL verdict, so the literal mismatch stays visible in the record rather than being interpreted away silently. This reading is named for veto in the seat's round report; if the maintainer orders the isolated-subagent route instead, the verdicts are re-run that way before any label is cleared. Either constant fix (bump, or a family/prefix floor) is the skills lane's, draft-only.

**Triage: `bug` · `priority:p1` · `pm:queue` · `domain:skills` · `needs:contract-review` · type `Bug`.** The `finding` label comes off — first grading. Four seats now, counting this one: the triage seat is served `claude-fable-5-1` too, so the literal mismatch holds here as well.

**Face verified on `origin/main` @ `72adb7f`:** `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs:7692` is `export const CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER = 'claude-fable-5';`. ✔

**p1, which is a grade the observation class does not usually get, for one reason:** the two corroborating comments record seats taking *different* postures on the same fuse — the `domain:cli` seat routes every Clause-② PR to an isolated at-tier subagent and refuses to self-clear, the `domain:spec` seat reads the fuse as the floor it was written to be and reviews in seat, with five Clause-② cards in flight under that reading (#13802 · #14106 · #14153 · #13671 · #13672). A governance fuse that two seats satisfy by two different procedures is not a stale string; it is a gate that no longer says one thing. That is worth fixing today.

## The scope is larger than the card records

The card names the constant plus two references. `SKILL.md` also **hard-codes the model name three times**, which the same file forbids:

- `SKILL.md:771` — 「档位以 dispatch-gates 常量 `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` 为准(档位单源,⛔ 本文与标签不写模型名,**模型升级只改一行一个文件**)」
- `SKILL.md:361` — `claude-fable-5` 分诊子代理 (urgent-card dispatch)
- `SKILL.md:589` — 强制条款① `model: "claude-fable-5"`
- `SKILL.md:597` — 语义面 …一律 `claude-fable-5`

So the "one line in one file" promise is **false today**: a refresh needs four literal edits across two files, and two of the three offenders sit inside the mandatory clauses. `references/lanes/director.md:13` complies (「⛔ 本文不写模型名」) and is the model for what the other three should look like. This enlargement is the part with lasting value — fixing only the constant leaves the promise broken and the next refresh re-opens the same divergence.

## The fork, and why only one limb is queued

The card offers two directions. They are not equivalent under the human floor:

- **Bump `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` to `claude-fable-5-1`, and make `SKILL.md` name the constant instead of the model** — pure restoration. The comparison stays exact, no gate accepts anything it did not accept by design, and the "one line in one file" promise becomes true for the first time. **This is what is queued.**
- **Make the comparison a family/prefix floor** (`claude-fable-5` accepting `-1` and later point releases) — this *widens the accept set of a governance gate*. Gate weakening is on the human floor, and it is on the floor precisely because the party proposing it here is the party the gate constrains. ⛔ Out of scope for this card; whoever takes it must not implement it, and must not "compromise" by doing the bump and the prefix together. If the recurrence at the next refresh proves annoying enough to be worth the widening, that is a `needs-user-decision` card with the four facets, not a dev-agent judgement call. Not filed today: zero pull until a refresh actually happens, and the bump plus the de-hardcoding removes the pain that exists now.

## What the bump does to the interim divergence

Both seats' postures converge the moment the constant names the served tier, forward. Backward, it also largely settles itself: the `domain:spec` seat's five verdicts were produced by a model at the tier the constant *should have named all along*, so the bump vindicates them in substance rather than by interpretation. ⛔ The triage seat does not rule on whether those five stand — that seat named its reading for veto in its own round report and the veto stays with the maintainer. This is recorded only so nobody reads the bump as a silent retro-blessing, or as a reason to re-run five reviews nobody asked for.

## Dispatch notes

- Clause ① applies (the change touches `SKILL.md`, a protocol semantic surface) ⇒ dispatch at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. `needs:contract-review` is applied because the change moves which model strings satisfy a gate.
- The recursion is real and has a boring answer: this card repairs the fuse that governs its own review, so a mismatch on the fuse cannot be grounds to stall it. Whichever posture the reviewing seat holds, write **both** strings — the served model and the constant's value — verbatim into the verdict, and the isolated at-tier subagent route with transcript verification is always available and never wrong.
- Governed surface (`scripts/pm/**`, `.claude/**`) ⇒ draft-only PR, no auto-merge.
- After the edit, re-grep for the model name across `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**` and `scripts/pm/**`: the acceptance test for this card is that `claude-fable-5` appears as a *value* in exactly one place.

Size/model suggestion: S, at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.
